standard.title: Phonic knowledge for complex words
standard.description: use phonic knowledge of common and less common grapheme–phoneme relationships to read and write increasingly complex words
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use phonic, morphemic and vocabulary knowledge to read and spell words that share common letter patterns (AC9E5LY08). They have not yet applied phonic generalisations to read and write words with uncommon letter patterns such as those in 'pneumonia', 'resuscitate' and 'vegetation'.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can apply phonic knowledge of common and less common grapheme–phoneme relationships to read and write increasingly complex words including those with uncommon letter patterns.

nodes.label: Common grapheme-phoneme relationships in complex words
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply phonic knowledge of common grapheme–phoneme relationships to read and write multi-syllabic complex words.
nodes.minimum_width: Decode and spell at least three provided complex multi-syllabic words by applying common grapheme–phoneme relationships; explain the phonics strategy used.
nodes.typical_width: Apply phonic knowledge to read and write a range of complex words; use knowledge of syllable patterns and common letter patterns to decode unfamiliar multi-syllabic words encountered in curriculum-area reading.
wider: Apply phonic knowledge to decode unfamiliar subject-specific vocabulary across curriculum areas
Compare how the same phoneme is represented by different graphemes in a set of related words and identify the pattern
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who have not achieved fluent decoding of common complex patterns cannot apply phonic strategies to the less common patterns in Node 2 — the cognitive load of slow decoding prevents pattern recognition for uncommon letter combinations.

response_modes.reason: Applying phonic generalisations to complex words requires fluent automaticity — the decoding needs to be fast enough that it does not impede reading comprehension. Repeated encounter and practice with complex words builds the fluency required.

success_criteria: Reads at least three provided complex words accurately by applying phonic strategies
Spells at least two provided complex words correctly

nodes.label: Less common grapheme-phoneme relationships
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply phonic generalisations to read and write words with less common and uncommon letter patterns.
nodes.minimum_width: Correctly read and spell at least two words with uncommon letter patterns (e.g. 'pneumonia', 'resuscitate') and identify the less common grapheme–phoneme relationship involved.
nodes.typical_width: Apply phonic generalisations to read and write complex words with uncommon letter patterns; use phonics knowledge to attempt unfamiliar technical and scientific vocabulary encountered in reading.
wider: Research the etymology of words with uncommon letter patterns (e.g. silent 'p' in Greek-derived words) and explain how knowing origins aids phonics decoding
Collect examples of uncommon letter patterns from curriculum-area reading and identify the pattern each represents
success_criteria: Reads at least two words with uncommon letter patterns correctly
Names the less common grapheme–phoneme relationship in at least one example

nodes.label: Phonic strategies in independent reading
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can independently apply phonic knowledge to decode unfamiliar complex words encountered during reading across curriculum areas.
nodes.minimum_width: Encounter and decode at least two unfamiliar complex words in a curriculum-area text using phonic strategies; explain the strategy used for one.
nodes.typical_width: Independently apply phonic knowledge (including less common grapheme–phoneme relationships) to read unfamiliar technical and scientific vocabulary encountered in curriculum-area reading; use phonic decoding as one strategy alongside context and morphemic knowledge.
wider: Collect unfamiliar words from curriculum-area reading and analyse the grapheme–phoneme patterns in each, building a personal phonic reference
Teach a classmate the phonic strategy for decoding a set of complex words from curriculum reading

response_modes.reason: Independent phonic decoding in real reading contexts integrates common pattern knowledge (Node 1) and uncommon pattern knowledge (Node 2) alongside contextual and morphemic cues — the coordination of multiple word-solving strategies is the integration challenge.

success_criteria: Decodes at least one unfamiliar complex word encountered during reading using a phonic strategy
